source: NIST Chemistry WebBook, SRD 69, 'Thermophysical Properties of Fluid Systems' (E. W. Lemmon, M. O. McLinden and D. G. Friend), https://webbook.nist.gov/chemistry/fluid/
query: https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/fluid.cgi with Action=Data, Wide=on, Digits=12, RefState=DEF, VisUnit=uPa*s, Type=IsoBar and TLow=THigh=T; each row is the single data row of the stored URL.

webbook_transport_models.parahydrogen: Viscosity: Muzny, Huber and Kazakov, J. Chem. Eng. Data 58:969-979, 2013 (normal-hydrogen correlation). Thermal conductivity: Assael et al., J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 40(3), 033101, 2011, with its critical enhancement.
webbook_transport_models.normal_hydrogen: Viscosity: Muzny, Huber and Kazakov, J. Chem. Eng. Data 58:969-979, 2013. Thermal conductivity: Assael et al., J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 40(3), 033101, 2011, with its critical enhancement.
webbook_transport_models.oxygen: Viscosity and thermal conductivity: Lemmon and Jacobsen, Int. J. Thermophys. 25:21-69, 2004.
webbook_transport_models.nitrogen: Viscosity and thermal conductivity: Lemmon and Jacobsen, Int. J. Thermophys. 25:21-69, 2004.
webbook_transport_models.methane: Viscosity: Quinones-Cisneros, Huber and Deiters, unpublished work, 2011. Thermal conductivity: Friend, Ely and Ingham, NIST Technical Note 1325, 1989, with their critical enhancement.
webbook_transport_models.helium: Viscosity: Arp, McCarty and Friend, NIST Technical Note 1334 (revised), 1998. Thermal conductivity: Hands and Arp, Cryogenics 21(12):697-703, 1981.

near_critical_note: Rows flagged near_critical lie within about 7 % of T_c at near-critical pressures (for hydrogen also one compressed-liquid row at 32.5 K, 1.3 MPa), where the conductivity critical enhancement is large.

lemmon_jacobsen_2004_table_v.source: Lemmon and Jacobsen, Int. J. Thermophys. 25:21-69 (2004), Table V, p. 28 (viscosity column header prints mPa s; the text, Eq. (1), gives uPa s)

assael_2011_table_7.source: Assael et al., J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 40, 033101 (2011), Table 7, p. 11 (rows without critical enhancement only: the 35 K, 30 kg/m3 row needs the background viscosity of REFPROP at the time, which is not printed)

friend_ely_ingham_1989_table_a1.source: Friend, Ely and Ingham, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 18, 583 (1989), Table A1, p. 630 (dilute-gas eta_0 from Eq. (10a), lambda_0 from Eq. (13a))

friend_ely_ingham_1989_table_a3.source: Friend, Ely and Ingham, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 18, 583 (1989), Table A3, p. 632 (single-phase region; density from their own equation of state)

muzny_2022_erratum_check_values.source: Muzny, Huber and Kazakov, Erratum to J. Chem. Eng. Data 58, 969-979 (2013): check values printed in the erratum (4-5 significant digits) for the hydrogen viscosity correlation, which is implemented from the CoolProp transcription.

skipped_rows.reason: WebBook returned 'undefined' for cv, cp, w, JT and k

conductivity_in_range_note: False for the hydrogen rows at 150 MPa: inside the Muzny et al. viscosity range (200 MPa) but above the Assael et al. conductivity range (100 MPa); viscosity only.

coolprop_transcription.used_for: Hydrogen viscosity (Muzny et al. 2013; JSON 'viscosity' blocks plus viscosity_hydrogen_higher_order_hardcoded) and helium thermal conductivity (Hands and Arp 1981; conductivity_hardcoded_helium). The primary papers were not opened; correctness rests on these transcriptions as verified against the WebBook rows of this file.
